predecessors.name: Maya city-states (Preclassic and Classic)
predecessors.text: Cobá, whose built-up area extends 'over some 80 km2' and which 'must have dominated a vast area'; the page gives no extent

successors.name: Chichen Itza
successors.text: Cobá reduced to its core after 'the emergence of powerful city states of the Puuc culture'

ledger.x: 201: 'Between 201 and 601 AD, Coba must have dominated a vast area'; 'Cobá was first settled between 50 BC and 100 AD' and grew strongly 'after 100 AD'.
After 600: 'the emergence of powerful city states of the Puuc culture' (page); the page gives no date for any particular loss, so 601 (the end of the 201-601 span) is a bridge.

About 950: 'Beginning around 900 or 1000 AD' Cobá declines, 'with the latter [Chichen Itza] dominating at the end as it gained control of key cities such as Yaxuná'; Cobá was reoccupied 'from 1200-1500 AD' and 'abandoned by the time the Spanish conquered the peninsula'.
